subject: VPC ephemeral snapshot lifecycle, residency guarantees, and SLAs
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@optimahealth.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: security@optimahealth.com
Date: 2028-11-07T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Questions on ephemeral snapshots & residency guarantees for VPC deployment

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. A couple of follow-ups from our security and infrastructure teams about the Private/VPC deployment model:

1) Ephemeral snapshots: if Redwood takes periodic ephemeral snapshots of the model inference cache or workloads (for warm-starts, debugging, or failover), can those snapshots be configured to land in customer-controlled object storage in our AWS account? If so, can Redwood commit to residency (region + account) for those artifacts and provide evidence they were deleted when requested?

2) Retention windows: we need clarity on the maximum retention for any snapshots or diagnostic bundles created by Redwood agents inside our VPC. Can this be policy-driven per workload and enforced by the control plane?

3) Proof of deletion: what level of evidence will Redwood provide when a snapshot or its copies are deleted (s3 object deletion logs, inventory, manifest, signed attestations)? Our auditors expect verifiable deletion timelines.

4) Contract language: can you share suggested contract/SLAs around snapshot residency and deletion (e.g., deletion within N hours of request, attestations within 5 business days)?

Appreciate a brief Q&A we can circulate to the team.

Thanks,
Lydia
Lydia Park
Head of Cloud Security, OptimaHealth

Subject: Re: Questions on ephemeral snapshots & residency guarantees for VPC deployment

Hi Lydia — thanks, good questions. Below is a concise Q&A + operational playbook for the scenarios you outlined. I'll also attach a proposed contract snippet in a follow-up message.

Q1 — Can snapshots be placed in a customer-controlled AWS account/region?
- Short answer: yes. For Private/VPC deployments we support directing any Redwood-created artifacts (ephemeral snapshots, diagnostics bundles, debug traces) to a customer-managed S3 bucket in your account. That bucket can be restricted to a single region (e.g., us-east-1) and must follow the usual bucket policies we agree on.
- Implementation note: we configure an IAM role in your account that our runtime assumes for object writes. No persistent credentials are stored in our control plane; we use short-lived STS tokens.

Q2 — Retention windows and policy enforcement
- Policy control: retention is configurable per "artifact class" (snapshot, cache-snapshot, diagnostic-bundle). You set the policy values via the Private Console or declarative YAML on the control plane (e.g., retention_days: 7).
- Enforcement: two-tier enforcement: (1) Redwood agents will expire and delete objects on the customer bucket according to retention policy, and (2) we also maintain a control-plane tombstone manifest (audit entries) showing the deletion action and associated object keys.

Q3 — Proof of deletion
- Evidence provided: when you request deletion we can supply: S3 object deletion events (CloudTrail/CloudWatch Event IDs), an inventory manifest showing removed keys, and a signed attestation (signed by Redwood key) listing keys and deletion timestamps.
- Timeframes: for synchronous deletions initiated by the customer, deletion actions are performed within the SLA window (see Q4). Generated attestations/documents produced within 5 business days by default; expedited attestations can be SLA'd.

Q4 — Suggested contract language & SLAs
- Proposed baseline: Redwood will delete customer-directed ephemeral artifacts within 24 hours of a verified deletion request and provide deletion evidence (inventory + signed attestation) within 5 business days. For high-priority deletion requests (severity P1), deletion within 4 hours and attestation within 24 hours can be added as an upgrade.

Operational caveats and security controls
- Immutable snapshots: if you enable object-lock/retention-legal-hold on your bucket we will honor it, but that will prevent deletion until legal-hold removed. We recommend not enabling object-lock for ephemeral artifacts unless required.
- KMS: objects written to your bucket can be encrypted with your KMS CMK. We support envelope encryption where Redwood never has access to your CMK.
- Snapshots copied out-of-band: we do not, by default, copy snapshots outside your specified bucket/account. Any required replication for durability must be explicitly authorized.

Next steps
- Dev will share the ops playbook and exact IAM role template. Naomi will prepare a short one-page contract snippet.

Cheers,
Priyom
Senior Product Manager — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Lydia — quick operational breakdown from the infra side below, with runbook attachments.

1) IAM/IAM role template: we will provide a least-privilege role that allows PutObject, GetObject, DeleteObject for a defined prefix (e.g., redwood/ephemeral/*). Example: sts:AssumeRole with external ID. We do not request ListBucket at the root unless you ask us to.

2) Deletion mechanics:
- Soft-delete step: Redwood agents mark an artifact DELETING in the control-plane manifest and emit the S3 DeleteObject.
- Verification step: after S3 reports success, we poll for object inventory (S3 Inventory / ListObjectsV2) and record the object absence in the manifest. If the bucket is configured for versioning, we also issue DeleteObjectVersion for the specific version IDs or call PutObjectRetention where applicable.
- Attestation generation: once verification passes, the runtime emits a signed attestation (PKCS7 signature) that contains keys, deletion timestamps, and our job run id.

3) Edge cases:
- If automated deletion fails (network, permissions), the object goes to a retry queue and we escalate to your designated operator; remediation timeline is configurable.
- For encrypted with customer CMK: if Redwood cannot perform DeleteObjectVersion due to KMS Deny, we'll surface the error and provide evidence of attempted action; final deletion requires CMK key policy update or manual action from your side.

Attachments: [attachment: ops-snapshot-runbook.pdf (application/pdf)]

If you want, we can run a dry-run by creating a test artifact, deleting it, and handing you the full attestation package.

- Dev

Hi Lydia — following up after internal alignment. Naomi attached a suggested contract clause below; feel free to request edits. Also looping in the HubSpot deal for the procurement thread.

Suggested contract snippet (editable):
"Redwood will, at the Customer's direction, write any ephemeral runtime artifacts (including but not limited to model cache snapshots, diagnostic bundles, and debug traces) to an S3 bucket under the Customer's AWS account and region. Redwood shall not copy such artifacts outside the configured bucket/account without prior written authorization. Upon receipt of a verified deletion request from the Customer, Redwood will delete the specified artifacts and any accessible copies within 24 hours, and provide an attestation describing the deleted object keys and timestamps within five (5) business days. For Priority-1 deletion requests, Redwood will perform deletion actions within four (4) hours and provide attestation within 24 hours. Deletion may be delayed if the Customer has enabled object retention or legal hold on the target S3 bucket; Redwood will notify the Customer and request removal of such holds to proceed with deletion."

If that looks good, Naomi will drop this into the redline template and we can move it into the SOW.

Best,
Priyom
